title: 4D Chicago Business
description: One business, one file, under data/businesses/. A business is an identity — a house of trade that persists across the window the sources cover — and this record is the place its people, its premises and its dates are written with a tier on each. The 196 records compiled from the newspaper register are DERIVED (tools/compile_businesses.py --build) and must not be hand-edited; --check re-derives them and refuses one that has been. Records authored by hand live under data/businesses/authored/ and are merged in by the same compiler. Semantic rules — a tier that requires sources, a person id that must resolve, a location that must name what it points at — are enforced by the compiler's self-test and by tools/validate.py.

tier.description: The grade ladder of data/residents/index.json .vocabulary.grades, unchanged. `attested` requires at least one source_id; `inferred` and `reconstructed` require a basis stating the reasoning.

date.description: ISO, to whatever precision the source gives. Null where the record does not bound that end.

role.description: Agrees with data/residents/index.json .vocabulary.relationships wherever a word appears in both, so a person's household role and their workplace role are the same word. The workplace-only additions (proprietor, bar_keeper, hostler, printer, teacher, cook, porter, labourer) are the roles T-1183's staffing model will fill. THE FOUR CIVIC OFFICES (T-1410) are not new words either: `postmaster`, `land_office_register`, `land_office_receiver` and `county_clerk` are already in .vocabulary.occupations, held there as what a man WAS, and a civic establishment needs them as what he DID at a place. One word for the office on the person and on the seat is the same rule this enum already follows for `clerk`.

name.description: The name as the source reads it. Never normalised away — the printed string is the evidence.

person_id.description: A town resident id (data/residents/), or null where the register could not match the printed name to a card. Null is a statement about the evidence, not a placeholder: `basis` says which.

register_person_id.description: The register's own id for the printed name, kept so a reader can walk back to the notice.

also_printed_as.description: The OTHER styles the same paper printed this same person under, folded onto this row by compile_businesses.fold_printed_styles on `person_id` — never on the name. "J. D. Caton" and "J. Dean Caton" are one partner of Collins & Caton, and Giles Spring was printed three ways. The typography is evidence and is kept here rather than deleted; what the fold removes is only the second COUNT of one man. Empty on every row but the twelve the register double-printed.

anchor.description: THE LANDMARK AN `anchored` LOCATION STANDS AGAINST, as an id rather than as a sentence. The register's `action_target`, resolved by compile_businesses.anchor_of: a committed structure (15), another house in this layer (7), or a crossing of two platted streets (4). It does NOT place the house — `structure_id` stays null on an anchored location, because the anchor is what the house stood next to and a roof of its own is precisely what the register could not give it.

id.description: A committed structure id or a `biz_` id. Null on a corner, which names two streets and no one thing.

title.description: What a card prints: the roof's name, the firm's name, or the two street names joined.

streets.description: The two street ids of a corner; empty otherwise.

kind.description: `anchored` is the register's `new_building`: the paper anchors the house against a landmark the town holds and the town holds no roof of the house's own, so the location is real and stops at the anchor. `street_only` and `unplaceable` are LIMITS, not places: the register found a street and no house, or no anchor at all. They are carried as locations so that the 61 street-only and 62 unplaceable businesses of the 1835 register are data a query can count, rather than prose in an action note.

primary.description: Exactly one location per record is primary.

limit_reason.description: Required on `street_only` and `unplaceable`: WHY the record stops where it does, in the register's own words.

id.description: Stable slug, matching the filename. `biz_` for an attested or inferred house, `rcb_` for a reconstructed one. The 196 compiled records take the register's own id with its `business_` prefix replaced, which is 1:1 with the printed notice; the parent ticket's `biz_<surname>_<trade>` form is reserved for records a human authors, because derived over the register it collides 27 times and every collision is an identity question tools/compile_businesses.py must not answer by itself.

register_id.description: The data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json business this record compiles, or null for an authored record with no printed notice.

name.description: The firm style as printed, or — for a reconstruction — a period form.

provenance.description: Where the record came from. `compiled_from_register` records are rewritten on every --build and a hand edit is refused.

type.description: The census classes of data/research/newspapers/trade_class_rulings.json — the ONE taxonomy, so a business counts against the December 1835 State census without a second crosswalk. A house may hold more than one. `civic` (T-1410) is the one class here the census does NOT enumerate, and that is the point of it: the State count of late 1835 runs through the trades and never reaches the post office, the land office or the county's own rooms, so a civic establishment counts against no census line and the crosswalk does not compare it. It is kept out of `other` because `other` means *the register printed a trade this enumeration has no line for*, and these three were never in the register at all.

trade.description: The printed trade, verbatim. Never replaced by the class.

occupation.description: The finer trade from data/residents/index.json .vocabulary.occupations, where the register derived one.

firm_styles.description: The house's own trading styles as printed — 'Clark, Filer & Co.' — kept apart from the people, because a style carries surnames and a surname pass that reads it as a person invents one.

staff.description: Empty on every compiled record: the newspapers name proprietors and partners and almost never a clerk. T-1183 rules the staffing model and T-1189 fills this.

evidence.description: The printing window, kept as it was: the dates the notice ran, which bound the record and are not the same claim as when the house opened.

exclusion.description: The register's exclusion, if the house is not in the July 1835 town.

proprietor_community.description: DERIVED FROM THE PEOPLE THE RECORD NAMES, never from a surname (T-1378, from T-1177). The vocabulary is now literally the resident layer's — data/residents/community_rules.json — rather than a second list that said it was shared and was not: that one folded New England, New York, British and Southern into one `anglo_american` and said `black` where the resident layer says `free_black`. Every record read `unattested` under it, so ending the divergence cost no record a reading. One set of terms for a house and for its keeper is what makes the Indian trade, the Metis houses and the Black-owned firms identifiable on one field. `unknown` is the honest answer where no keeper on the record carries a community, and it is a pill in the Businesses view rather than a hidden row.

tier.description: The weakest of the contributing keepers' own tiers, CAPPED AT `inferred`: a person's community is evidence about the person, and a house is not its keeper. Null where the value is `unknown`.

rule.description: Which of the four cases fired. Two of them are silences and are told apart on purpose: `no_community_on_the_people_named` is a gap in the resident layer, `no_person_linked` a gap in the register.

from.description: Every proprietor or partner the resident layer holds a card for, with the community that card carries — the whole of what the value was read off. Staff are not read: a clerk's community is evidence about the clerk, not about the house that employed him.

claim_ids.description: The newspaper claim ids the record rests on, so every line walks back to a quoted printing.

survival_required.description: Documented before the scene date and assumed still standing on it.

backdating_required.description: Documented only after the scene date and assumed already open on it.

replaceable_by.description: What evidence would retire this record or this reading — the standing instruction to the next researcher.

reconstruction.description: PRESENT ON A RECONSTRUCTED HOUSE AND ON NOTHING ELSE (T-1184). The contract the reconstruction programme puts on a reconstructed PERSON, asked of a firm: WHAT BOUGHT THIS HOUSE, which group of which programme wrote it, the seed string a reader can retype to redraw every drawn value on it, and what retires it. A record carrying `provenance: "reconstructed"` and no block here cannot say where it came from. TWO ways a house is bought, and a record states exactly one: a QUOTA ROW (`bucket` + `slot`), where the order book counted a shortfall against the register; or a DOCUMENTED FLOOR (`floor`), where the corpus states the count directly and no bucket exists to name — T-1377's Black-owned firms stand on Andreas's 1833 certificates of freedom, and the programme that would mint a barber bucket (T-1186) has not run (owner, 2026-09-19). tools/compile_businesses.py refuses a record naming both or neither and holds a floor to its own count, sources and argument; tools/reconstruct_businesses_1835.py --check re-derives every quota row from its seed and refuses a hand edit.

group.description: The reconstruction group: one of the five the business band cuts the order book into, and the unit one ticket builds.

ticket.description: The ticket that owns the order-book rows this group fills — the book's own `owning_ticket`, never restated by hand.

bucket.description: The order-book bucket key that ordered this house.

slot.description: The slot within that bucket. Stable across builds because the book's order is, which is what makes the seed reproducible.

floor.description: A DOCUMENTED FLOOR, in place of a quota row: a count the corpus makes directly, which this house stands for. It carries its own evidence, because nothing upstream counted it — there is no order-book row to point at.

as_of.description: The date the reading is of.

sources.description: Source ids. A floor nothing states is an estimate, not a floor.

note.description: The argument that carries the count to the scene date.

why_a_firm_and_not_only_a_person.description: Why the floor buys a FIRM and not only the person it counts.

seed.description: The seed STRING every drawn value on this record hashes with blake2s — a reader can retype it and redraw the firm style, the goods line and the street face.

basis.description: The shape T-1158 fixed on every reconstructed value: `model` where a table decided it, `rule` where a stated rule did.

withdrawn_if.description: What retires this house. The same standing instruction the reconstructed trade heads carry, in the same words.
